definition: Passive resistance is an indirect way of expressing hostility by resisting or avoiding demands rather than opposing them openly. In the packet, it appears as part of a broader pattern of negativistic attitudes and reduced cooperation in social and work situations.

provenance.scope: Source record C34904; pinned source text

reasons: The definition’s claim that the term “appears as part of a broader pattern of … reduced cooperation in social and work situations” is not supported by the packet text. The packet mentions negativistic attitudes and indirect hostility/passive resistance to demands for adequate performance, but does not mention reduced cooperation.

The definition adds unsupported wording and implications: the packet says “passive resistance to demands for adequate performance” and “indirect expression of hostility,” but it does not explicitly support “avoiding demands” or “rather than opposing them openly.”

“Reduced cooperation in social and work situations” is not stated in the packet; the packet instead says “negativistic attitudes and passive resistance to demands for adequate performance in social and occupational situations.”
